waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Vellfire or an MG M9, wait for Denza's 13 Nov debut. The D9 electric luxury MPV is expected around ₹80–90L, but prices and the sale date may come later than the unveil.
notes: BYD's premium Denza brand debuts in India on 13 Nov 2026 (confirmed by BYD). Reports say the Z9 GT shooting brake and the D9 MPV come first, both as imports; Autocar India's November list names only the Z9 GT for that date. D9 price is an estimate (Autocar Pro: about ₹90L; others ₹80–90L). Global D9 EV: 103 kWh, about 520 km WLTP.

waitAdvice: This is a niche, very fast electric shooting brake with no direct rival in India. Wait for the 13 Nov unveil only if a ₹1.2 crore-plus EV is on your list.
notes: Denza's India debut model on 13 Nov 2026. Global spec: 122.5 kWh, three motors, 1,156 hp, about 600 km WLTP, 0–100 km/h in 2.7 s. Autocar India estimates ₹1.2–1.5 crore. Listed as 'coupe' because the schema has no shooting-brake body. India-spec figures not announced.

waitAdvice: If you want a small premium EV, the new-generation Cooper SE launches on 27 Nov alongside a Paul Smith Edition. Wait for the price; the old model sold for about ₹53–55L.
notes: Launch reported for 27 Nov 2026. Global spec: 54.2 kWh, 218 hp / 330 Nm front motor, 402 km WLTP, 95 kW DC charging. No India price announced yet.

waitAdvice: If you want a 7-seat EV and are looking at the XEV 9S or Harrier EV, the Safari EV was expected by Diwali but has not launched. Newer reports say early 2027, so don't hold off a purchase for long.
notes: Part of Tata's FY2027 plan. Expected to carry over the Harrier EV's 65/75 kWh packs and RWD/AWD layouts. It missed the Diwali 2026 window; as of 7 Nov 2026 Tata had given no date, and newer reports point to early 2027. Aggregator price guess is about ₹32L.

waitAdvice: If you're about to book an Innova Hycross, wait about three weeks: the facelift is reported for 25 Nov 2026 with a new nose and a 12.3-inch screen. Don't take pre-facelift stock without a big discount.
notes: Autocar India (3 Nov 2026) reports a 25 Nov launch; other outlets say 26 Nov. Toyota had not officially announced the date. Already launched in Indonesia. Expected: new grille, headlamps and bumpers, 12.3-inch touchscreen, 12.3-inch digital cluster on hybrids, and possibly a flex-fuel (E30+) strong hybrid. Price range is Autocar India's estimate. The Maruti Invicto will likely follow.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Virtus, wait. The facelift is due in December 2026 and gets the 8-speed automatic already given to the Slavia and Taigun facelifts.
notes: Volkswagen has revealed the facelift; reports say it is unveiled in late Nov and launched in early Dec 2026, no exact date yet. Keeps the 1.0 and 1.5 TSI; the 1.0 TSI automatic moves from 6 to 8 speeds. Expected to mirror the Slavia facelift: new lighting, 360-degree camera. Price range is an estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Fortuner or Gloster, JSW's boxy plug-in-hybrid Combat is unveiled on 4 Dec. Sales and deliveries may come later, and it's a new brand with an unproven service network, so weigh that.
notes: JSW Motors' first car, a 5-seat plug-in hybrid based on the Chery Jetour T2. Unveil on 4 Dec 2026 (an unveil, not confirmed as the on-sale date). 1.5L turbo-petrol plus two motors, 18.4 kWh battery, 360 hp / 610 Nm, about 90 km NEDC electric range (Jetour T2 figure). Autocar India expects ₹40–50L. Listed as 'strong-hybrid' because the schema has no PHEV fuel type.

waitAdvice: This is a boxy, retro-styled EV from a new brand. Only worth waiting for if you like its looks; established rivals are on sale now.
notes: Spied testing in India. Global range 401/510 km by battery. Listings say 15 Nov 2026, but reports point to late 2026 to 2027 after JSW's Maharashtra plant starts.

waitAdvice: If you want a tiny city EV like the Comet or Tiago EV, VinFast's VF3 micro-SUV is expected around Nov 2026 at about ₹7.5–10L. Wait to see its price.
notes: VinFast has confirmed the VF3 for India in 2026, but as of 7 Nov 2026 had given no date or price. CarWale's tentative listing says Nov 2026; earlier dates have already slipped. Two-door micro SUV; 18.64 kWh, about 210 km (NEDC) in global spec.

waitAdvice: This is a possible low-cost alternative to the Punch EV and Nexon EV around Nov–Dec 2026, but the date is unconfirmed and VinFast's service network is thin.
notes: Listings give 17 Nov or Dec 2026 at about ₹10–12L. No OEM date.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Creta Electric or e Vitara, BYD's smaller Atto 2 may arrive in Dec 2026, but the date isn't confirmed.
notes: Listings say about 15 Dec 2026, with estimates from ₹16.99L or ₹18–25L. BYD also teased its first PHEV (Seal U DM-i) in June 2026.

waitAdvice: This is a coupe-SUV EV that could undercut the Curvv EV, but Citroen's dates have slipped before. Don't hold off a purchase for it.
notes: Spied testing. Listings say mid-Dec 2026 at ₹14–17L (earlier expected Nov 2025). As of 7 Nov 2026 there was no Citroen announcement; the latest Basalt news is the petrol X Comfort Edition (Jul 2026).

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Fronx, the facelift is listed for Nov 2026 and is due by Mar 2027 at the latest. Wait, or demand a big discount on current stock.
notes: Maruti had not announced a date as of 30 Oct 2026 (91wheels). Listings say Nov 2026; IndiaTV/Carlelo say by Mar 2027. Expected ADAS and styling updates. The strong hybrid follows separately (see maruti-fronx-hybrid).

waitAdvice: If you drive a lot and are about to buy a sub-4m petrol SUV, Maruti's in-house series hybrid (claimed 35+ kmpl) should arrive in H1 2027. It's worth waiting for if fuel cost matters most.
notes: Debut of Maruti's in-house series hybrid (Z12E 1.2L as generator). Spied testing. Expected to be among India's most affordable strong hybrids. Price not known.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Grand Vitara, a facelift with Level 2 ADAS is reported by Mar 2027. Negotiate hard on current stock or wait.
notes: Reported mid-life update with Level 2 ADAS and minor design changes, existing powertrains. Target 'by March 2027' per reports.

waitAdvice: If you need 7 seats but want hybrid-level fuel economy, Maruti's 3-row Grand Vitara is expected in late 2026 to 2027. Worth waiting a few months for.
notes: Codename Y17. Stretched Grand Vitara with a third row, petrol and strong hybrid. Name unconfirmed; 'Escudo' is registered. Timing has slipped repeatedly. A Toyota (Hyryder-based) version is also expected.

waitAdvice: If you want a 7-seat EV under ₹20L, Maruti's e Vitara-based electric MPV is expected in H1 2027. Wait if Maruti's network matters to you.
notes: Shares e Vitara's platform and batteries; spied testing. No official date; estimates run from Q1 to mid-2027. CarTrade estimates ₹14–18L. A Toyota version is expected.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Punch EV or another sub-₹13L EV, Hyundai's Inster-based compact EV is confirmed before Mar 2027. Wait a few months to compare.
notes: Hyundai India CEO confirmed launch within FY2026-27 (by Mar 2027); reportedly fast-tracked. Built at Sriperumbudur. Early cars use Svolt cells, later Exide. India-spec range not announced. Price is an Autocar estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Creta petrol, the next-gen car (with a strong hybrid expected) is due in 2027, and a reveal may come late 2026. Wait if you can, or get a big discount and keep the car long.
notes: Spied testing. Hyundai confirmed the next-gen Creta for India at its 2026 Investor Day. Most reports say early 2027 (CarWale: Mar 2027); Autocar suggests it could be H2 2027. Expected 1.5L strong hybrid (possibly later). Creta Electric refresh also due in 2027.

waitAdvice: This is not worth waiting for yet. The project has reportedly gone quiet, and the 3-row Grand Vitara and Nissan 7-seater are closer.
notes: Codename Ni1i. Planned to sit above the Alcazar as Hyundai's first India hybrid, built at Talegaon. Autocar India says the project has gone quiet; the date is uncertain.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Fortuner, the all-new one debuts globally on 1 Dec 2026 with India sales expected in 2027. Unless you need it now, wait to avoid buying the outgoing generation.
notes: Global debut confirmed for 1 Dec 2026; India launch expected 2027, reportedly after the Innova Hycross facelift. India powertrains unconfirmed; mild-hybrid diesel is likely given the current 48V Neo Drive.

waitAdvice: If you're spending ₹35–50L on a premium EV, Tata's Avinya is due in H2 FY27, possibly at the 2027 Bharat Mobility Expo. See it before deciding.
notes: Tata's first born-electric skateboard platform; likely a large SUV. Tata guides H2 FY2027; some reports say FY28. Price is an aggregator estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Tiago or Tiago EV, Tata plans a facelift this financial year (EV with the new 6-in-1 drivetrain). Ask for a large discount on current stock or wait.
notes: Part of Tata's FY27 plan (Tigor already replaced by the Aeris). Tiago EV test mules spotted.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Nexon, the all-new generation arrives around mid-2027. Buy now only at a strong discount and if you'll keep it 7+ years.
notes: Codename Garud, spied testing. Reports say Q2/mid-2027. May move to the ATLAS (Curvv) platform; diesel may be dropped; EV follows later.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Harrier EV or Sierra EV, Mahindra's boxy BE 07 is confirmed for 2027, likely H1. Compare it if you can wait.
notes: INGLO platform; 60–80 kWh packs reported. Mahindra ED Rajesh Jejurikar confirmed calendar 2027 (slipped from Oct 2026). Price is an Autocar estimate.

waitAdvice: If you want a rugged, boxy sub-4m SUV, Mahindra's 'baby Scorpio' on the new NU_IQ platform is spied with production lights and is expected in 2027. Worth a short wait.
notes: First NU_IQ model; built for petrol, diesel, hybrid and EV. Timing estimates run from Dec 2026 to mid/Aug 2027. Price is an Autocar estimate.

waitAdvice: Don't wait for this: the hybrid is still 'under evaluation'. Buy the current petrol or diesel XUV 7XO if it suits you.
notes: A series-parallel strong hybrid is reportedly in development; earlier '2026' and 'Nov 2026' reports did not pan out. The ICE XUV 7XO launched 5 Jan 2026.

waitAdvice: If you're looking at an Isuzu V-Cross or Hilux, Mahindra's Scorpio N-based lifestyle pickup is confirmed by April 2027.
notes: Mahindra confirmed launch by April 2027. Price is an Autocar listing estimate.

waitAdvice: Don't hold off a Thar Roxx purchase for this. The NU_IQ-based Thar.e/Vision T is likely late 2027 or even 2028, despite some listings saying Nov 2026.
notes: Vision T is the evolved Thar.e concept on NU_IQ, with EV and ICE versions. Some aggregators list 15 Nov 2026; better-sourced reports say late 2027 to early 2028.

waitAdvice: If you want a hybrid Seltos specifically, Kia has confirmed one for India in 2027 (likely late). Otherwise buy the current Seltos or a Duster or Grand Vitara hybrid now.
notes: The new-gen Seltos (launched Jan 2026) gets a strong hybrid; the US version comes first in late 2026. Kia says India gets it in 2027. Price is an Autocar estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Sonet and keep cars a long time, the next gen (with a hybrid) is reported for 2027. Push for a discount on the current one.
notes: Reported in Kia's 2027 plan alongside the Seltos hybrid. No OEM date.

waitAdvice: If you're a Honda loyalist eyeing a mid-size EV, the production model is revealed on 2 Dec 2026, with sales expected in 2027. Wait for its battery, range and price before you commit to a rival.
notes: Honda Cars India confirmed the name 'Alpha' and a 2 Dec 2026 world premiere in India. It is built in India for domestic sales and export. The reveal is not a price announcement; bookings, battery and range are not yet announced. Price is an aggregator estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy an Alcazar or Safari, Nissan has confirmed a 3-row SUV (Renault Boreal cousin) for Q1 2027. A short wait gets you one more option.
notes: Nissan India confirmed Q1 2027 at the Tekton launch. Built in Chennai. 1.3 turbo petrol expected; 1.8 strong hybrid reported. 6/7 seats, Level 2 ADAS expected.

waitAdvice: If you like the new Duster but need 7 seats, its 3-row sibling is confirmed for 2027 with turbo petrol and strong hybrid. Wait rather than squeeze into a 5-seater.
notes: Spied testing. Renault confirmed it for India; reports say early 2027 (Autocar's page says late 2026). Estimate ₹15–25L.

waitAdvice: This is a boxy sub-4m SUV from Renault, due mid-to-late 2027. Too far away to delay a Punch or Exter purchase.
notes: Renault-confirmed for 2027; sources say mid or late 2027. An EV version is listed for late 2027. Price is a ZigWheels estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Kylaq, VW's own sister SUV is confirmed for 2027. Only wait if you prefer VW styling, because the mechanicals will be the same.
notes: Volkswagen officially confirmed a sub-4m SUV on MQB-A0-IN (Kylaq platform) for 2027; related to the Brazil-market Tera. Name unconfirmed.

waitAdvice: Not worth waiting for unless you specifically want a plug-in hybrid. Timing and pricing are unclear.
notes: Wuling Starlight 560-based plug-in hybrid (and possibly a 56.7 kWh EV) spied testing; earlier targeted Jul–Oct 2026 and now likely 2027. Part of JSW MG's six-model 2026–27 plan. 'strong-hybrid' stands in for PHEV in this schema.

waitAdvice: If you're looking at an MG Astor or ZS EV, both are due for replacement on SAIC's SIGMA platform in 2027, so buy only with a big discount.
notes: Team-BHP reports next-gen Astor and ZS EV in 2027 on the SIGMA platform.

waitAdvice: If you want a Tesla but not an SUV, the Model 3 has been in homologation since 2025 but has no date. The Model Y and Model Y L are what you can actually buy.
notes: Homologation initiated in March 2025. The Model Y L 6-seater is already on sale at ₹61.99L. Price is an aggregator estimate.

waitAdvice: If you're about to buy a Range Rover and want an EV, the electric version is listed for around March 2027.
notes: Listings say Mar 2027 at ₹3–3.7 crore (estimate). The Range Rover Sport Electric is listed for a similar time.
